title: Gulf Coast hotels, Smackover tour, Halfway House and the band's breakup
summary: The Owls open hotels on the coast, tour Arkansas and play in rough Smackover, play the Halfway House, then break up as members return to careers; Eddie Miller sat in.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Then we left there, and went to Victory Inn, played at Victory Inn, for, uh, quite a little time, and we left there, and went to, uh, to the, uh, Edgewater Gulf Hotel, in, uh, in Black Sea, we opened that hotel up, we opened up also another hotel, in, in Gulfport, because we didn't play there, we only played there the opening night, and, uh, I can't think of the name of that hotel, but anyway, we,
Was it near the Markham Hotel, in that area?

It was the Markham Hotel, we opened that up, the new Markham Hotel, in our barnstorming days, uh, when we were playing with the Strand Theater, this is quite an incident, uh, we, uh, had a tour during the summertime, went all up through the country, up into North Louisiana, Mississippi, even up to Arkansas, uh, playing, playing, one night stands, in various theaters, and we got to a place, called, uh, let's see, it was up here in Arkansas, uh, well anyway, we played a theater there, and we were supposed, supposed to play a dance, the same night, the two dates were, the two times were conflicting, and, I didn't know whether we'd get out of there, safely or not, but we finally managed to play both of the engagements, and then we had an engagement to play in a town called Smackover, Arkansas, and, when we got through playing the dance, went to the hotel, we asked the fellow how far Smackover was, he said it was 15 or 18 miles, said, well we thought we'd ride it at night, he said, I wouldn't do that if I were you, he said, they hold him up every night between here and Smackover, and he says, if they don't have anything on him, tell him to go back and get it, he said, I don't think you fellas ought to ride up there during the night, so we waited until the next day, and then we got into Smackover, and Smackover was the funniest town I've ever gone into in my life, I'll tell you, it was an oil town, it was a boom town in those days, and that's a long time ago, it was right in the middle of Prohibition, in the middle of the street as we drove in, they had an enormous beer barrel up there, whether it had beer in it or not, I don't know, but it was the most rough and tumble town I've ever been in my life, and we were supposed to open a country club there, and this country club was, opening of the country club was supposed to be a, a dance where they paid so much admission, and we were supposed to get a percentage of the admission, we later found out that it was strictly a membership deal, and only so many people were allowed to come, and we couldn't possibly make any money out of it, no matter, if everybody came, it was supposed to come, but we got out of there, and got back safely, and that was before we went into the Roosevelt, and to get back after we finally, we left the Edgewater Gulf Hotel, we came back, and we went out to what was called the Halfway House, remember the Halfway House here, it's still out there now, but I think it's, it's Orkins now, or some such place, I think Brunus had been playing in there before we were, and we took that place over, and played out there for quite a while, and then, some of the boys in the orchestra, like Rainier Jalpe, and Siegfried Christensen, who was a pianist, he was a young chap, they decided they were going back, to complete their college education, that they'd had, as much as they wanted of music, they'd made a little money, that would get them through college, and they did, they went back, Rainier went back, and completed his education, as an architect, and Sieg Christensen, who was a married man at that time, went back and became a lawyer, and he's a lawyer in town today, and it was right after that, that the, the bands broke up, we all went, I got married, and went into business, my wife said, if you're going to play music, you're not going to marry me, because I don't want you to run around, all the country every night, so we broke up at that time, some of the boys went on, to play, at, suburban gardens, I think it was, Earl Crumb, and a few of the others, but it's very interesting, some of the chaps, that are in the, big time now, that have played with us, on various occasions, either as substitutes, or as, well, part-time fellows, that were with us, for, Eddie Miller for one, when we were at the Owl's Nest, as we'd call it, Eddie Miller was with us, as, as a saxophonist, at that time, Eddie went on, to be with, one of the, top notches, Nappy Lamar, I don't know whether, you ever heard of Nappy Lamar, he is, he is now out in Hollywood, I think, played, guitar with us, and made a recording with us, the Owls, the, the, the, Throwing the Horns, record was made, with Nappy Lamar, in, in there.
